newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica bails out ailing financial services sector.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica bails out ailing financial services sector.

text.p: Jamaica has set aside $182.6 million to bail out the nation's ailing financial services sector, Finance Minister Omar Davies said.

The government assistance, to be used during the remainder of the 1996-97 financial year ending March 31, was to be used to assist banks and insurance companies, according to the broad outline of a rescue plan announced by Davies Tuesday.
The money will be channeled through a new entity, the Financial Sector Adjustment Company. Davies said more money should be available in the 1997-98 fiscal year.

High interest rates, an increasing number of non-performing loans and a downturn in both the local equities and commercial real estate markets have caused a number of large financial companies to post big losses, prompting calls for government assistance. The situation is a major turnaround from what prevailed just a few years ago, when the financial services sector showed double-digit annual growth and was the fastest growing sector in the Jamaican economy.

The finance minister said further details would be made available next week. However, officials said the new entity will purchase stock and real estate portfolios, take equity stakes in ailing companies or a combination of both.
